hero.headline: Digital twins for *industrial decarbonisation*.
hero.name: Gift Eno Udoh
affiliations: PhD, Green Industrial Futures — Heriot-Watt University
hero.abstract: I am a multidisciplinary engineer working at the intersection of **energy systems, sustainability and process engineering**. My PhD builds **digital twins** to help decarbonise industry using **hydrogen and low-carbon energy vectors**, quantifying how distributed generation and storage change the cost, carbon and operational profile of a site. My MSc modelled **energy storage for large-scale solar farms**, and my earlier work spans food and process engineering. I care about reproducible modelling: every figure I publish should trace to a committed dataset and a re-runnable model. I am also building **DecarbTwin**, a digital-twin platform that turns this research into a decarbonisation-planning tool for energy-intensive SMEs (Converge KickStart 2026, top 50).

sections.title: Research
sections.lead: Digital twins for decarbonising industry with hydrogen and low-carbon energy vectors.
sections.body: My PhD (Green Industrial Futures, Heriot-Watt) develops digital twins to help decarbonise industry with hydrogen and low-carbon energy vectors — coupling data, physics-based component models and optimisation to compare supply and storage options over realistic operating years. My published work includes induction-heated catalyst systems for converting intermittent renewable power into hydrogen and hydrocarbons (Faraday Discussions, 2026). Alongside this I use PyPSA to model distributed storage (battery, hydrogen, thermal) and PV self-consumption in commercial settings, quantifying the cost, carbon and peak-demand trade-offs of each configuration.

sections.title: DecarbTwin
sections.lead: A digital-twin platform helping energy-intensive SMEs find their fastest, cheapest route to net zero.
sections.body: DecarbTwin lets a business input its operational data and compare decarbonisation pathways — hydrogen, electrification, renewables and energy storage — side by side, with **costs, carbon savings and matched incentives**. It targets a real and urgent market: Scotland has 1,295 food-and-drink manufacturers (96% of them SMEs) and 148 whisky distilleries consuming ~3.7 TWh a year, 72% still from fossil fuels — and from 2026 large buyers are mandating supply-chain emissions data. The platform is developed directly from my PhD digital-twin modelling at Heriot-Watt. **Shortlisted (top 50) in the Converge KickStart Challenge 2026.** *(Founder.)*
